events.title: Alexander Selkirk Is Rescued
events.description: Scottish sailor Alexander Selkirk was picked up by Captain Woodes Rogers and his crew. He had spent more than four years alone as a castaway on an uninhabited island in the Juan Fernández archipelago off Chile.
events.significance: His story is widely thought to have inspired Daniel Defoe's novel Robinson Crusoe, and it became one of history's best-known tales of survival.

events.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Signed
events.description: The United States and Mexico signed the treaty that ended the Mexican-American War. Mexico gave up large territories in the present-day American Southwest and West.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the map of North America. The United States gained land that became California, Nevada, Utah and parts of several other states.

events.title: First Groundhog Day in Punxsutawney
events.description: In Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, residents held the first American Groundhog Day celebration. Townspeople looked to a groundhog to predict how long winter would last.
events.significance: The event grew into a beloved annual tradition. It now draws crowds and media attention from around the world.

events.title: Ulysses Is Published
events.description: James Joyce's novel Ulysses was published in Paris on the author's 40th birthday.
events.significance: Many critics regard it as one of the most important works of modernist literature. It changed what a novel could do with language and structure.

events.title: Stalingrad Falls Silent
events.description: The last German forces at Stalingrad surrendered to the Red Army, which ended one of the longest and bloodiest battles of World War II.
events.significance: The defeat was a turning point on the Eastern Front. It ended German offensive momentum in the Soviet Union.
